rows.text: Compare glucose between CHO-004-R01 and CHO-004-R02

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
The two runs track each other closely: CHO-004-R02 runs slightly lower on glucose than CHO-004-R01 through the batch (right minus left, mean −0.24 g/L, sd 0.32 g/L over 11 matched sample times from 0 to 142 h). The largest gap is at 19.5 h: CHO-004-R01 at 7.133 g/L vs CHO-004-R02 at 6.189 g/L (−0.94 g/L); CHO-004-R01 dips to 6.428 g/L at 28 h, so they converge again by 44.5 h (6.59 vs 6.11 g/L). From 68 h onward the two differ by ≤0.28 g/L at each shared time, and both deplete to well under 1 g/L at 142 h (CHO-004-R01: 0.709 g/L; CHO-004-R02: 0.368 g/L). CHO-004-R01 has one extra sample at 164 h (0.124 g/L) with no counterpart in R02.

Caveats: these values are from the Northfield October delivery, which is still in review — they were read from the delivery files but not yet checked, and the delivery has open verification checks. Product, process version, equipment, scale and stage are not recorded for these batches, so the comparison is descriptive only; no cause is established. (Mean/median/sd are descriptive statistics from the comparison, not significance tests.)

rows.text: Why is glucose different between CHO-004-R01 and CHO-004-R02?

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
What the records show — the difference is modest, and CHO-004-R02 ran slightly lower almost throughout:

- Across 11 matched sample times (0–142 h), R02's glucose was below R01's at 9 of 11 points; the mean difference was −0.24 g/L (R02 minus R01, descriptive only).
- The largest gap was early: at 19.5 h, R01 was 7.133 g/L vs R02 at 6.189 g/L (−0.94 g/L). After that the runs tracked each other within ~0.2–0.5 g/L (e.g. 92 h: 4.227 vs 4.058; 142 h: 0.709 vs 0.368).
- R01 has one extra late sample at 164 h (0.124 g/L) with no R02 counterpart.

Why — I cannot say from these records. The delivery has no batch context recorded (product, process version, equipment, scale and stage are all not recorded), so I can't attribute the early gap to feeding, inoculum, or equipment differences, and I found no deviation or case records linked to these batches. The largest difference at 19.5 h, when both runs were otherwise near their peak, is the point a cause-hunting review would start with; the feed added parameter isn't in this October delivery, so feed timing differences can't be checked here.

Two caveats: these values are from a delivery still in review (provisional — read from the files, not yet checked), and this comparison is descriptive only, not evidence of a cause. Getting the feed records and batch context for these two runs from Northfield would be what settles it.

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
Glucose in **CHO-007-R01 ran on average ~0.21 g/L higher than CHO-007-R02** across the 9 matched sample times (0–146 h), but the two runs track each other closely. Both start near 7.6–7.8 g/L and fall steadily to ~0.2 g/L at harvest. The biggest gap is early: at 18 h, R01 was 7.83 g/L vs R02's 7.275 g/L (−0.555 g/L); at 114 h the gap was −0.388 g/L (2.464 vs 2.076). At 146 h: 0.22 vs 0.161 g/L. Only one time point (0 h) had R01 below R02.

Caveats:
- These values come from the Northfield November delivery, which is **provisional — read from the files and not yet reviewed**, so verify before relying on them.
- R01's 44 h sample (6.957 g/L) is unmatched because R02's 44 h value has **conflicting duplicate measurements that need source review** — that's the one open data issue.
- This is a descriptive comparison only; batch context (product, process version, equipment, scale, stage) is not recorded in this delivery, so no conclusion can be drawn about why the runs differ.

rows.reply:
The records don't establish a cause — here is what the data shows. **Note: all values are from the November Northfield delivery, which is still in review (unreviewed); nothing has been accepted by a reviewer.**

**What the data shows (glucose, g/L, same elapsed hours):**
- Both runs track nearly identical profiles: from ~7.6–7.8 g/L at inoculation (t=0 h) declining to ~0.16–0.22 g/L by 146 h.
- R02 is consistently lower than R01 after the first sample: mean difference −0.21 g/L across 9 matched timepoints (derived from the comparison output).
- Largest gap is at **18 h: R01 = 7.83 g/L vs R02 = 7.28 g/L** (0.56 g/L difference) — after that the divergence narrows (e.g., 90 h: 4.33 vs 4.20; 146 h: 0.22 vs 0.16).
- R01 has one unmatched sample at 44 h (6.96 g/L) that R02 doesn't have, and there is a **conflicting duplicate for R02 glucose at 44 h** requiring source review.

**What I could not establish:** I ran a cause-screening task and it found no linked records or closed cases that could explain the gap — no hypothesis is supported or ruled out. The records also don't note product, process version, equipment, scale, or stage for these batches, so I can't attribute the difference to a documented condition (e.g., differing feed profiles or cell density).

**What would help settle it:** resolving the 44 h duplicate, comparing feed added and viable cell density between the two runs (both in this delivery), and completing the review of this delivery, which has 79 open checks (missing fields, layout changes, etc.) that should be closed before relying on these values.

rows.text: Compare glucose between CHO-010-R01 and CHO-010-R02

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
Glucose in the two runs tracked closely through the first ~120 h and then diverged: CHO-010-R01 fell faster late in the run.

- Both started around 7 g/L and declined steadily to about 4.9 g/L at 117 h, with R01 slightly ahead in depletion (e.g. 6.27 vs 6.05 g/L at 41 h).
- The largest divergence was at **193.5 h: 2.72 g/L (R01) vs 3.87 g/L (R02)**, a difference of 1.15 g/L. R01 ended at 1.11 g/L at 209 h, while R02 reached 1.74 g/L at 209 h and 1.09 g/L at 217.5 h (that last R02 point has no matching R01 sample).
- Across the 16 matched times, the mean difference (R02 minus R01) was 0.17 g/L (derived statistic from the comparison), with R02 higher in 9 of 16 paired samples.

Two caveats: these values come from the Harborview CDMO delivery that is **still in review**, so they are unreviewed as read from the files. Also, batch context (product, process version, equipment, scale) is not recorded for these runs, so the late-run divergence can't be attributed to any specific condition yet.

rows.text: Why is glucose different between CHO-010-R01 and CHO-010-R02?

timing.basis: answer_seconds runs from when the message was sent to when this answer was saved; waiting_seconds is time queued or between retries.

rows.reply:
**Short answer: the records show a real measured difference, but no cause is established.** Both runs are in the Harborview fed-batch delivery, whose values are still in review (provisional, read from the delivery files but not yet checked), so everything below is unreviewed.

What the glucose data show (all at matched elapsed hours):
- At 0 h: CHO-010-R01 = 7.104 g/L vs CHO-010-R02 = 6.838 g/L — R01 started ~0.27 g/L higher.
- Mid-run they track closely (differences mostly under ~0.3 g/L; e.g. 117 h: 4.929 vs 4.889 g/L).
- From ~140 h onward R02 runs higher: +0.47 g/L at 140 h, +0.57 g/L at 160.5 h, and the largest gap +1.15 g/L at 193.5 h (R01 = 2.717 vs R02 = 3.865 g/L); at 209 h it is +0.63 g/L. R02 also has one extra sample (217.5 h, 1.085 g/L) not present in R01.

Candidate explanations, none proven:
1. **Feeding differed.** R01 received more cumulative feed at every matched time after feeding began (e.g. at 140 h: 363.2 g vs 334.6 g; at 328.5 h: 854.9 g vs 815.4 g) — a persistent ~30–40 g gap. Counterintuitively, the run with *more* feed has the *lower* late-run glucose, so feeding alone does not explain the late divergence unless feed concentration/composition also differed.
2. **Different consumption rates.** Viable cell densities are broadly similar (peak ~16.1 × 10⁶ vs ~16.2 × 10⁶ cells/mL), but R01's cells were higher at 160.5–169 h (15.4 vs 14.5 and 16.1 vs 15.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL) — potentially higher glucose uptake exactly when the gap opens.
3. **Batch context is not recorded.** The comparison's context check found no product, process version, equipment, scale or stage for either batch, so run-to-run differences in those conditions cannot be ruled out.

What would settle it: reviewing the provisional delivery first, then pulling the batch records' feed recipe (concentration, not just cumulative grams) and any notes on sampling/assay timing from the CMO — the difference definition here is R02 minus R01 at identical measured elapsed times, with no clock or phase alignment inferred.

This comparison cannot say why glucose differs: it shows the difference but establishes no cause. Across 11 sample times matched exactly from 0.0 h to 142.0 h, CHO-004-R02 read lower than CHO-004-R01 by a mean of 0.2392 g/L (median 0.242 g/L), and CHO-004-R02 was higher only at 0.0 h and 28.0 h. The largest gap was 0.944 g/L at 19.5 h, CHO-004-R01 7.133 g/L against CHO-004-R02 6.189 g/L. Product, process version, equipment, scale and process stage are not recorded for either batch, so the two runs cannot be assumed to share conditions. All 23 measurements come from a provisional delivery still in review, with 55 open checks. Explaining the difference will therefore require the batch records and the completed review.

**Possible explanations to check**
- CHO-004-R02 may have run under different conditions, such as other equipment, scale or process version, shifting glucose relative to CHO-004-R01. Check: Retrieve the batch records for CHO-004-R01 and CHO-004-R02 and compare product, process version, equipment, scale and process stage.
- A feed or sampling event near 19.5 h in one batch may account for the largest single gap of 0.944 g/L. Check: Review the run logs and feed records for both batches around 19.5 h.
- Data quality may contribute to the apparent difference, since none of the values has completed review. Check: Finish the delivery review, exclude any rejected values, and repeat the comparison on accepted values.

**What this cannot tell**
- Whether the mean shortfall of 0.2392 g/L is statistically meaningful, since successive samples of one run are not independent and no significance test is reported.
- What CHO-004-R02 glucose did after 142.0 h, since it has no sample matching the 164.0 h point of CHO-004-R01.
- Whether the open review will change any of the 23 values used here.
